welcome.label: Welcome · the star party

parts.label: 🔎 The case question
parts.title: What should Sam bring?
parts.body: The town can rent ONE tool. Can every wish come true?

welcome.script:
(Look up, like you’re searching the night sky.) Have you ever made a wish on a star? Today four kids made wishes about the stars.

[ON SCREEN: Four wishes]
The red tide is gone, and Palmetto Beach is throwing a star party. Read these four wish cards. Which one sounds hardest to you?

[ON SCREEN: The case question]
The town can rent just one tool. Press Listen on Sam’s walkie-talkie, right below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · race the light (Clue 1)

parts.label: 💬 The claim
parts.title: Starlight is older than you
parts.body: The starlight you see tonight left its star before you were born.

warmup.script:
[ON SCREEN: The claim]
Here’s a claim: the starlight you see tonight is older than you. Thumbs up if you think that’s true. Thumbs down if it’s false.

[ON SCREEN: The farthest one]
This is the Andromeda Galaxy. You can see it from a dark place in Florida as a faint fuzzy patch. How long ago do you think its light left? Make your guesses, then send the light. Press Listen.

part1.label: Part 1 · open wider (Clue 2)

parts.label: 🔍 The trick button
parts.title: Zoom only
parts.body: Does zooming in show any NEW stars?

part1.script:
(Make a tiny circle with your finger and thumb, then a big circle with both hands.) Which one would catch more rain? Light works the same way.

[ON SCREEN: Your light catcher]
Drag the gold dot to open the opening wider, and count the stars.

[ON SCREEN: The trick button]
Then try Zoom only. Watch closely. Did you get any new stars? Press Listen.

part2.label: Part 2 · find it in the sky (Clue 3)
part2.script:
[ON SCREEN: Leo’s wish]
This is what Leo wants to see. Aim each tool at Saturn and the other wishes. Which tool shows the rings? Which one fits the whole star cluster? Press Listen.

explore.label: Part 4 · stare at nothing (Clue 4)

parts.label: ⬛ An empty speck
parts.title: A grain of sand at arm’s length
parts.body: Hold a grain of sand out at arm’s length. That’s how much sky Webb stared at.

explore.script:
(Pinch your fingers like you’re holding a grain of sand, and hold your arm out.) This tiny! That’s how much sky we’re about to look at.

[ON SCREEN: An empty speck]
To your eyes it looks empty. Try binoculars and the telescope too.

[ON SCREEN: After 12.5 hours]
Here’s a sneak peek. Then press and hold Webb’s shutter until all 12 and a half hours pass. Press Listen.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: What should Sam bring?
parts.body: Pick the plan that fits all four clues.

parts.label: ✍️ Your case report
parts.title: Three places to write
rows: Three views of one far-away thing

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
You have four clues. Crack the case at the top of this tab.

[ON SCREEN: The permit map]
Then Sam’s permit opens. This is Florida at night, from space. Where would the stars be easiest to see?

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Then write your case report: two short answers, three views for Part C, and your CER. Press Listen.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The claim
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “We don’t need telescopes in space. Just build them taller on Earth.”

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
[ON SCREEN: The claim]
A classmate says we can skip space telescopes. Just build them taller! Hmm. Would a taller telescope get above the air? Did zooming in show new stars?

There’s no wrong side, as long as you prove it.

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Tap your side and two facts, then explain how they prove your claim. Try starting with “This shows that…” Press Listen.

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 🎟️ Your specimen
parts.title: Star party ticket
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: ➡ Next week
parts.title: Motion and energy
parts.body: How does energy make things move?

closing.script:
Case closed! Every kid gets their wish, because you matched each wish to the right tool.

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist, and your star party ticket goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next week]
Next week Sam’s tools get a new job: energy and motion. Press Listen for Sam’s last word.

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.
